p: Dean Oliver Barrow was born on 2 March 1951 in Belize City, then in British Honduras, where he grew up. He attended St. Michael's College in Belize, took a law degree at the University of the West Indies at Cave Hill in Barbados in 1973 and a Certificate of Legal Education at the Norman Manley Law School in Jamaica in 1975, and later studied at the University of Miami.

He entered the legal profession in 1974, working with his maternal uncle Dean Lindo, and became a partner in Lindo's firm in 1977. He later founded his own firm, Barrow and Williams, with Rodwell Williams. Among its more controversial clients were Lord Ashcroft and his associated businesses, including Belize Bank and Belize Telemedia Limited.

Barrow entered electoral politics in December 1983, winning a seat on the Belize City council as one of a slate of nine. In 1984 he stood for the newly created Queen's Square constituency, defeated Ralph Fonseca of the People's United Party and joined the first cabinet of Manuel Esquivel as attorney-general and minister of foreign affairs. He held his seat in 1989, when his party lost power, and became deputy leader in 1990 after the death of Curl Thompson. Back in government in 1993, he added the ministry of national security to his former posts; his detractors called him Minister of Everything.

In the heavy defeat of 1998 he was one of only three party candidates to win, and he replaced the defeated Esquivel as party leader and Leader of the Opposition. The general election of 7 February 2008 gave his party 25 of 31 seats, and he was sworn in the next day as the country's first black prime minister, serving also as minister of finance. He won a reduced majority in 2012 and a third consecutive victory in November 2015, which he said would be his last election as leader.

Citing his health, he at first intended to step down by the end of 2019, but on 18 November 2018 his cabinet urged him to stay until the general election of 2020, and he agreed. He did not contest Queen's Square in that election and endorsed his sister, Denise Barrow, to succeed him. He has returned to private practice as head of litigation at Barrow and Williams. His eldest son, Moses Michael Levi Barrow, a former rapper under the name Shyne, was elected to the House of Representatives in 2020 and later became leader of the party and of the opposition.
